page: Amazon Web Services m8in.32xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with dedicated Intel x86_64 processors operating at frequencies up to 3.9 GHz. The compute architecture provides 64 physical cores and 128 virtual CPUs, backed by 512.0 GB of system memory. This yields a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core, which matches typical general-purpose sizing profiles.

Network performance is a central attribute of this instance variant, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data volumes and file systems must be provisioned externally over Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) or network storage fabrics. Compute acceleration hardware is also excluded, as there are zero GPUs present.

In terms of operational efficiency, the instance provides dense compute capability and high network throughput within a unified large-footprint footprint. Workloads requiring massive network I/O avoid multiple smaller virtual machine bottlenecks. However, applications requiring low-latency scratch disks must account for network transit overhead, as all disk operations traverse external storage.

The m8in.32xlarge is built for network-intensive, compute-heavy, and balanced business workloads. Primary target applications include large relational database engines, enterprise resource planning systems, high-traffic web serving fleets, distributed caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines processing significant data transfers.
description: Amazon Web Services m8in.32xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and dedicated Intel x86_64 processors clocked up to 3.9 GHz. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores, paired with 512.0 GB of system memory to maintain a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A defining characteristic of the configuration is its 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating large data flows and inter-node communication. The instance contains no dedicated GPUs and features no local instance storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize network-attached block or object storage. Because of its dense core count, large memory footprint, and enhanced networking capacity, the instance operates efficiently for distributed systems, multi-tiered enterprise software, high-throughput web serving, and large-scale relational databases relying on external volume architectures.
